WHAT IT IS
- Tesla’s paid autonomous ride service. You book a car in the Robotaxi app. The car drives. There is no human driver on unsupervised rides.
- Live cars today are mostly Model Y. The purpose-built Cybercab is the volume vehicle testers say Tesla is prioritizing.
- Camera-only vision. Tesla VP of AI Ashok Elluswamy: no lidar, radar, or HD maps required for safe operation on this stack.
- This how-to merges the public Robotaxi service folder with Owning Robotaxi Fleet (owner / private-fleet economics). Not Cybercab-only bookmarks.

HOW IT WORKS
- Download the Tesla Robotaxi app and join the waitlist. Official robotaxi (Sep 2025): app is available to all; access expands over time.
- Book the ride in Tesla’s app. Elon: Tesla will not partner with Uber or Lyft. “We will have enough demand.”
- Unsupervised means no safety driver. Supervised cities still have a person in the car.
- Official robotaxi (Aug 27): service hours are 6am to 10pm, 7 days/week. Unsupervised fleet is a lot bigger. Upgraded vehicle distribution and routing so you wait less.
- Testers: you can change destination and keep the same trip for multiple stops.
- Cars return to a depot or homebase and park themselves (Houston footage).
- Ashok: FSD v15 is already running on Model Y robotaxis and will run on Cybercab.
- Testers: Tesla is limiting Model Y conversions to prioritize Cybercab, built with an unboxed modular process.
- Testers (Aug 24): Tesla expects Cybercab to replace Model Ys in the Robotaxi fleet over time and become the highest-volume vehicle there. Testers flag Sept 3 / 9/3 as the Cybercab strategy moment. Austin public Cybercab rides described as “imminent.”

HOW TO USE
- Official robotaxi: download the app, join the waitlist.
- Official robotaxi (Aug 27): rides run 6am to 10pm every day. Unsupervised fleet is a lot bigger; routing upgrade is meant to cut wait time.
- Testers: booking is in the app. One Orlando rider paid with an X Money card.
- Tesla site (as quoted): app in 29 languages; service animals; space for some wheelchairs and assistive devices.
- Testers: vehicles in Nevada must be marked “Robotaxi.”
- After the Aug 20 Nevada approval, testers say Tesla still has to finish vehicle inspections, insurance, and published rates before paid rides start there.

OWNING / FLEET (from Owning Robotaxi Fleet dump)
- Elon (Feb 2026, also in Robotaxi folder): Tesla owners will be able to add their cars to the Robotaxi network; Tesla collects 25% of revenue.
- Fleet testers frame the network like Airbnb for cars: owner adds vehicle; Tesla handles software, routing, payments, rider experience; platform fee often modeled ~25–35%; owner keeps the rest after operating costs (tester).
- Fleet / Teslaconomics (Mar 2026): ~$30k/yr net profit per Robotaxi to owner is a base-case assumption from analyst models + Tesla long-term vision — after platform fee, charging, tires, maintenance, insurance, cleaning. No official real-world owner earnings in this dump. Profit/mile chatter ~$0.25–$0.50 after costs at 50k–100k+ miles/yr in high-demand areas.
- Fleet / Teslaconomics: Cybercab cost chatter ~$25k–$30k; Elon told that tester production was starting in ~1 month (Mar 2026 context — treat as dated tester claim). Rough capital for a ~$1M/yr fleet ~$850k–$1M in vehicles (tester arithmetic).
- Fleet / chamath: intends to buy and deploy large fleets nationally when possible; expects payback and positive FCF in under 2 years (tester / investor claim, not Official Tesla).
- Fleet / BrianRoemmele: “all in” on buying into the owning-fleet thesis now; separate Optimus ownership program mentioned but not published in this dump.
- Fleet / tslaming (Mar 2026): then only 8 unsupervised Austin robotaxis — historical; do not use as current fleet size (Robotaxi dump Aug 23 tester: 908 total).
- Testers / Teslaconomics (Aug 25, Robotaxi folder): “owning your own Tesla Robotaxi fleet can one day make you financially free.” Still a tester slogan — no Official owner-earnings number in this dump.
- CONFLICT / caution: owner earnings, Cybercab sticker, ROI, and payback are tester models. Dump explicitly says none of it is guaranteed. Do not treat as Official Tesla guidance.

text:
In the summer of 1965, a telephone call reached a struggling Saab dealership in West Barnstable, Massachusetts.

The man who answered was 43 years old, nearly broke, raising six children, and writing science-fiction novels that most literary critics dismissed without a second thought.

His name was Kurt Vonnegut.

On the other end of the line was writer Vance Bourjaily, calling on behalf of the University of Iowa's famed Writers' Workshop. A teaching position had unexpectedly opened, and they wanted to know if Vonnegut would be interested.

The salary was $8,500 a year.

Vonnegut didn't hesitate.

He said yes.

That decision would alter the course of his life.

Within two years, he would complete the novel that finally made him a literary star, mentor young writers who would become major voices in American literature, and step across the invisible boundary separating an overlooked novelist from one of the most influential authors of the twentieth century.

But by then, he had already endured more than enough hardship for one lifetime.

The path to Iowa had been anything but easy.

In December 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge, the 22-year-old Vonnegut was captured by German troops. Months later, while imprisoned in Dresden, Germany, he survived one of the most devastating bombings of World War II.

As Allied planes turned the city into an inferno on February 13–14, 1945, Vonnegut and fellow prisoners survived by sheltering deep underground inside a meat locker beneath a slaughterhouse.

When they emerged, Dresden was gone.

For weeks afterward, they were forced to recover bodies from the ruins.

The experience would haunt him for the rest of his life.

The war wasn't the only tragedy waiting for him.

While he was overseas, his mother took her own life the night before he was due home on leave. By the time he returned to America, he was carrying grief that would never fully leave him.

And yet he spent the next twenty years trying to do something that seemed impossible:

Write honestly about Dresden.

Every attempt failed.

The memory was too fractured, too painful, too enormous to fit into a conventional story.

Meanwhile, life kept moving.

He married Jane Cox, his childhood sweetheart, in 1945.

He worked in public relations for General Electric in Schenectady, New York.

He wrote short stories for magazines.

He published novels one after another:

Player Piano in 1952.

The Sirens of Titan in 1959.

Mother Night in 1961.

Cat's Cradle in 1963.

God Bless You, Mr. Rosewater in 1965.

Critics often praised his imagination but rarely treated him as a serious literary figure. Most simply placed him in the science-fiction category and moved on.

Then life dealt another devastating blow.

In September 1958, Vonnegut's sister Alice died from cancer just two days after her husband was killed in a tragic commuter-train accident.

Their children suddenly had no parents.

Without hesitation, Kurt and Jane took in three of Alice's four sons.

Their family expanded overnight from three children to six.

The responsibility was enormous.

By 1965, Vonnegut was struggling to support everyone. Book royalties weren't enough. The Saab dealership wasn't succeeding. Money was tight, and the future was uncertain.

Then came the call from Iowa.

The Iowa Writers' Workshop was already one of the most respected creative writing programs in America.

For Vonnegut, it offered something priceless:

Stability.

For the first time in years, he could breathe.

He arrived in Iowa City carrying manuscripts, unfinished ideas, and the emotional weight of a war he still hadn't managed to put on paper.

What followed were two of the most important years of his life.

He taught fiction from 1965 to 1967.

Among his students was a young writer named John Irving, who would later become one of America's most celebrated novelists.

Irving never forgot him.

He once described Vonnegut as a man who was harsh toward institutions but deeply compassionate toward individual people.

Others remembered him the same way.

His classes weren't casual obligations.

He cared.

Students remembered his comments decades later. They remembered his humor, his honesty, and his insistence on clarity.

While helping young writers find their voices, Vonnegut finally found the form his own long-delayed book required.

For twenty years he had tried to write about Dresden as a straightforward war story.

It never worked.

Then he realized the memory itself wasn't straightforward.

Trauma doesn't unfold in neat chronological order.

It jumps.

It circles back.

It revisits moments without warning.

That insight changed everything.

He created Billy Pilgrim, a man who becomes "unstuck in time," drifting across different moments of his life.

Through Billy, Vonnegut finally discovered how to tell the story he had been carrying since 1945.

In Iowa City, he finished Slaughterhouse-Five.

At the same time, attitudes toward his work began to shift.

A major review in Harper's treated him as a serious literary writer for perhaps the first time.

His Iowa salary increased from $8,500 to $11,000.

Publishers and critics suddenly seemed more interested.

People who once ignored him began paying attention.

He left Iowa in 1967.

Two years later, Slaughterhouse-Five was published.

Vonnegut was 46 years old.

The timing was remarkable.

America was deeply divided by the Vietnam War, and readers were already questioning the purpose, cost, and consequences of conflict.

Vonnegut's novel arrived at exactly the right moment.

The response was explosive.

Almost overnight, he became one of the most widely read writers in the country.

The book has remained a classic ever since and is regularly included among the most important English-language novels of the twentieth century.

The man who had spent decades struggling for recognition had finally broken through.

He went on to write many more books.

He became one of the most recognizable literary voices in America.

Yet throughout his life, he kept returning to a simple belief that mattered more to him than literary fame:

"God damn it, you've got to be kind."

It was advice he repeated often because he believed it.

After everything he had seen—war, death, loss, disappointment—kindness remained the lesson he valued most.

Kurt Vonnegut died on April 11, 2007, at age 84 after suffering injuries from a fall near his Manhattan home.

In the years that followed, former students, friends, and fellow writers reflected on the impact he had made.

John Irving remembered him.

Suzanne McConnell remembered him.

Countless others did too.

And many of them traced a crucial turning point back to one unlikely decision:

Accepting an $8,500-a-year teaching job in Iowa because he needed a way to support six children.

What looked like a temporary lifeline became the bridge to everything that followed.

A struggling writer.

A family in need.

A two-year teaching appointment.

And one book he'd been trying to write since he was twenty-two years old.

Sometimes history changes not with a grand moment, but with a phone call answered at exactly the right time.

text:
A stay from the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court would pause Judge Sullivan’s planned mistrial declaration in the Lindsay Clancy trial.1
The jury is hung after a third deadlock note. The defense wants the SJC to review whether the trial judge should have taken other steps first—such as individually questioning or removing the reported holdout juror who allegedly refused to follow instructions on reasonable doubt, sending the jury back again, or requiring any partial verdicts the panel had already reached on some charges.15
If the stay is granted, the mistrial does not take effect immediately and the current jury remains in place while the higher court decides. If it is denied (or if the hour expires without one), the mistrial stands. Clancy stays in custody, and prosecutors then decide whether to retry the case, offer a plea, or drop the charges. A hung-jury mistrial is not an acquittal, so double jeopardy does not bar a second trial.

More than 50,000 Jewish worshippers gathered Thursday night at the Western Wall, below Jerusalem’s Temple Mount, for a central Selichot prayer service, crying out for God’s mercy and forgiveness ahead of the Feast of Trumpets and Yom Kippur.

The Western Wall Heritage Foundation said more than half a million worshippers have taken part in Selichot services at the Western Wall Plaza since the beginning of Elul, the Jewish month traditionally marked by repentance, prayer, and preparation for the High Holy Days. During the gathering, prayers were also offered for Israel’s soldiers and security forces, along with appeals for national unity and the peace and security of Israel.

The scene carried deep biblical weight. Thousands stood shoulder to shoulder in Jerusalem, facing the stones nearest the ancient Temple courts, seeking mercy before the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For generations, the Western Wall has remained a place where Jewish hearts return in sorrow, hope, and longing.

The prophet Zechariah speaks of a coming hour, when the Lord will pour out “the Spirit of grace and supplication” upon the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. What was seen last night in prayer may be only a shadow of the day when Israel’s tears will become a fountain of cleansing, and Jerusalem will no longer be known for war, but for the mercy of God and the return of the King.

text:
Dear CM Vijay - Why not explore mobile jammers inside major Hindu temples?

This is a follow-up to my quoted post on the merits and demerits of the mobile phone ban in major Hindu temples.

Instead of asking devotees to pay ₹5, deposit their phones and stand in long queues, why not explore the use of government-approved mobile jammers within designated temple premises?

Devotees could still carry their phones with them, but calls, mobile internet, livestreaming and other network-based distractions would stop working once they enter the jamming zone.

Of course, this would not stop people from taking photographs or recording videos offline, so strict enforcement of photography restrictions would still be required.

For emergencies, temples could have clearly marked non-jamming zones near the entrance or other designated areas where devotees can use their phones. People have the right to access their phones during emergencies.

This could still solve several practical problems.

People would not have to surrender expensive smartphones. There would be no need to queue up to deposit and collect them. Elderly devotees and families could keep their phones with them for emergencies and transport once they step outside the restricted zone.

Of course, mobile jammers are strictly regulated in India and would require the necessary permissions and technical safeguards before deployment.

But that is precisely my point.

Since this is a ‘young’ Cabinet, why not explore technology and other innovative solutions before inconveniencing lakhs of devotees with a blanket surrender-of-phones policy?

@tnhrcedept should seriously examine whether authorized jammers, strict photography enforcement, designated phone-use zones and proper emergency arrangements could offer a smarter solution.

Technology should solve the problem without becoming another problem for devotees! @CMOTamilnadu @RameshOffcl

text:
Is CM Vijay turning anti-Hindu by banning camera phones in major temples? Some questions and thoughts!

This is a very sensitive and touchy topic, so I have exercised caution with my choice of words while sharing my own experiences and expressing my opinion. Many may not agree with me. So, feel free to agree to disagree respectfully.

First and foremost, I would love to raise a fundamental question here - Why do we visit temples?

To me, a temple is a place where a devotee is in unison with the Divine, and I feel there is absolutely no need for a phone. I personally hate seeing people click photos inside temples.

And they won’t stop with one pic or video. They regroup, rearrange themselves and go for multiple takes. Some even try to take pictures of the Moolasthanam, only to be yelled at by the Archakas. Still, they continue clicking selfies with God, which I abhor.

Having said this, I can understand why many are infuriated with CM Vijay for bringing in this mandate. But I feel there are both merits and demerits to this decision by the government.

Merits!

1. They may want to prevent people from using temple premises for selfies as though temples are picnic spots.

2. At least banning camera phones means no cringe videos are made inside temple premises.

3. That said, no camera phones could also mean that people who visit temples primarily to make reels may think twice before going, while genuine devotees will still visit.

4. You can hardly sit peacefully or meditate after a darshan these days. Phones keep ringing. Some have crappy item numbers or rap music as ringtones, while others keep their phones at annoyingly high volumes.

Demerits!

1. Photographs taken by devotees can sometimes serve as time-stamped evidence for records. But one could argue that every major temple has professional photography sessions, and official photographs of the temple and deities are uploaded on their respective websites.

2. Without camera phones, devotees may have less ability to document theft, damage or other wrongdoing involving jewellery and statues. But temple administration miscreants can probably do their mischief with or without phones. Despite CCTVs, there have been multiple instances of jewelry and statues being stolen.

3. Why has HR&CE banned camera phones alone? What if devotees need to capture something such as poor facilities or administrative lapses and produce it as evidence?

Now, following up on that fundamental question, I have a few more questions!

A. Will a ban on bringing camera phones into temples stop Hindus from visiting temples?

If yes, I feel that is a lame argument because genuine devotees probably won’t care. In that sense, CM Vijay’s decision to ban camera phones may actually be seen as a show of respect towards both temples and genuine devotees.

Perhaps it may even encourage devotees to visit smaller temples that have the same spiritual energy but don’t get the attention they deserve. I personally love visiting smaller temples with fewer crowds, where I can chant my mantras and meditate peacefully.

B. However, why allow non-camera phones at all? How many people even use non-camera phones in this day and age?

If phones in general are a distraction, allowing phones without cameras defeats the very purpose of banning phones. Tirumala Venkateswara Temple bans even smartwatches for security reasons and other purposes.

C. Why should devotees have to pay money to deposit their phones at the entrance?

I find this atrocious. Why can’t the temple administration provide this facility free of charge, even if it means longer queues? This may definitely dissuade some people, especially elderly devotees, from visiting temples.

Also, smartphones are not used only to take photos, shoot videos, attend calls or send messages. They are also used to make digital payments to arrange transport. All of this could get disrupted.

D. Is the blanket ban a good decision?

Maybe... Maybe not. I feel the required infrastructure could have been developed and deployed before bringing in the ban.

E. Were there other ways of addressing some of the demerits listed above?

Absolutely.

A better approach could have been strict enforcement of phone usage within temple premises, accompanied by heavy penalties for improper usage. 

For example, in Singapore, you can carry your phone to make calls and send messages, but photography is generally restricted to permitted areas in places of worship. If you break the rules, you would be fined a bomb.

F. But is it possible to enforce such strict rules consistently in a democratic country like India?

I don’t know... I really don’t know.

As Annamalai said, ‘keep your faith at home while you step out’, perhaps it may be wise to keep our phones at home while we visit temples. 

If the temple is near your house, you can walk to and fro without a phone. But otherwise?

G. So, is this ban a good step?

It certainly has some merits.

H. Could the government have avoided a blanket ban?

Perhaps, but only if workable alternatives could first have been found and implemented, and the required infrastructure deployed.

To conclude!

One should not forget two simple facts -

1. Similar rules are already in place in temples such as the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, Tiruchendur Subramaniya Swamy Temple and Ramanathaswamy Temple in Rameswaram. So, this is not entirely new to devotees!

2. Devotees were visiting temples, praying, meditating and connecting with the Divine long before mobile phones ever existed!

Beginning in Charleston, this Southern U.S. tour saunters through the Spanish moss-draped coast of South Carolina and Georgia. Clippity-clop down the mansion-lined lanes of picturesque Beaufort in a horse-drawn carriage. Board an open-air trolley to discover the famed squares of storied Savannah. Walk in the footsteps of Vanderbilts and Rockefellers at the once ultra-exclusive Jekyll Island Club. This Small Group Discovery tour is the perfect way to discover Southern hospitality served with a sweet side of delicious pecan praline.

Special features included in this tour:
• Guided sightseeing in Charleston including the Battery and Rainbow Row

Day 1
Your Small Group Discovery Tour begins!

EXPLORE MORE in Charleston with a visit to the new International African American Museum, a stroll at the waterfront, or discover the South Carolina Aquarium. Your Tour Director has suggestions for your free time, and your GlobusGO mobile app puts all the possibilities right at your fingertips.
CITY SIGHTS From Rainbow Row to the aroma of honeysuckle flowers on the French Quarter and the Battery promenade to the pastel-painted antebellum homes along the cobblestone streets, the sights of historic Charleston are a feast for the senses. Horse-drawn carriages lumber down the avenues as they have since the city’s founding in 1670 and carry passengers to the Waterfront Park overlooking Charleston Harbor, while Fort Sumter still stands where the first shots of the Civil War rang out across the water.
Day 2
Heart of Low Country
Start the day with a city tour of Charleston. Continue to America’s most photographed plantation, Boone Hall Plantation and Gardens, for a guided tour including a Gullah presentation. This afternoon, tour Patriot Points Naval Museum for a hands-on look at retired aircraft, naval carriers, and a Vietnam Experience Exhibit. Enjoy the afternoon at your leisure. You may wish to shop for a favorite souvenir at the historic Charleston City Market, where more than 50 artisans are on-site daily; visit Fort Sumter National Monument, take a relaxing and scenic cruise of Charleston Harbor; or try one of Charleston’s favorite dishes, such as shrimp and grits, barbecue, or coconut cake.
Enjoy a dinner of southern specialties at Globus Local Favorite a favorite local restaurant.
breakfast
dinner
LOCAL TASTES No visit to Charleston is complete without good old-fashioned Southern cooking. Pull up a chair for made-from-scratch Southern classics in a local eatery. Charleston is known for traditional Lowcountry specialties, local seafood, and the delicious Lady Baltimore cake.
HISTORIC SITE Tour the mansion with a guide, see the beautiful gardens and the Black History in America exhibit at historic Boone Hall Plantation - one of America’s oldest working farms. Once known for cotton and pecans, the farm still actively produces strawberries, tomatoes, peaches, and other signature Southern produce on the banks of Wampacheone Creek where it has stood the test of time since its founding by the Boone family in 1681.
Day 3
Sights of the Civil War
Depart Charleston for picturesque Beaufort, a town that has conserved much of its pre-revolutionary character. Tour the town by Globus Local Favorite horse-drawn carriage through narrow, oak-lined streets past the former homes of wealthy cotton growers. This afternoon, continue to romantic Savannah, America’s first planned city.
breakfast
SMALL GROUP EXCLUSIVE Explore Beaufort in style with a Local Guide on a horse-drawn carriage. The coastal town’s historic district has well-preserved Antebellum and Victorian architecture including homes that pre-date the Civil War. Learn about Beaufort’s role in the Civil War, the Lowcountry history, and local favorite sites used in movies such as Forrest Gump and The Prince of Tides.
SMALL GROUP EXCLUSIVE ACCOMMODATION The River Street Inn blends modern boutique hotel comforts with the storied past of a two-hundred-year-old cotton warehouse, overlooking the Savannah River in the heart of the Landmark District. Immerse yourself in the Southern hospitality, historic cobblestone streets, cultural charm, and vibrant riverside atmosphere.
Day 4
Southern Hospitality
Explore Savannah on a trolley tour led by a Local Guide who will entertain you with stories of the city’s legendary characters and past. Discover more in the historic district with a small group exclusive private tour of the Mercer Williams House Museum, the mysterious setting for the book and film, Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil. The remainder of the afternoon is at leisure. Tonight, experience Lowcountry cuisine during an Globus Local Favorite interactive cooking class and dinner, infused with memorable stories and special southern flavors.
breakfast
dinner
SMALL GROUP EXCLUSIVE Discover the charm and captivating stories of Savannah where Southern cuisine, art, period architecture, and local fables fill the air under a cool veil of Spanish moss that drapes the oaks of this historic and unforgettable city. Experience the tastes of the South during your hands-on cooking class and take-home memories, plus recipes, from your visit to Savannah.
Day 5
Golden Georgia Coast
Depart Savannah for the Golden Isles of Georgia. Discover the remarkable scenery and island tales at St. Simon’s Island Lighthouse & Museum. Enjoy an island fare lunch and continue to Jekyll Island for a relaxing 2-night stay at the Jekyll Island Club. Enjoy the rest of the day at leisure in the resort. Your Tour Director will have suggestions for dining this evening.
breakfast
lunch

Delight in the atmosphere and superior service of this famous resort. Explore walking trails, paved bike paths, and croquet games while at the beachfront resort.
Day 6
Trolleys & Timeless Tales
Enjoy a leisurely start to the day and a guided trolley tour of the Jekyll Island Historic District. A cluster of 19th-century winter-cottages, this “club” was formed by some of America’s most prominent families. The rest of the day is yours to explore the island. Perhaps take a boat ride, shop, or kayak close to the sandy coast. Your Tour Director hosts an elegant farewell dinner at the Jekyll Island Club to celebrate your Southern adventure.

Happy 45th Birthday to the gorgeous, massively talented, chart-topping, record-breaking, history-making, Singer, Songwriter, Dancer, Record Producer, Actress, Entrepreneur and Fashion & Global Icon, the Legendary One & Only #Beyoncé!💪🎂🎉🌟🐐👑🤍
Named by Billboard as the Greatest Popstar of the 21st Century, Beyoncé has transformed Pop and R & B more than almost any other artist over the last 25 years! Her true superpower is forcing the entire industry to treat pop music as high art and changing how pop stars operate! She's one of the best-selling Artists of All time, having sold over 300 million records worldwide including her work as a solo artist, and as the lead singer of the chart-topping, history-making, top-selling legendary R&B girl group Destiny's Child! Beyoncé is one of the Greatest Singers and Entertainers of All Time, famous for her distinctive three octave mezzo-soprano vocal range and for having one of the most powerful live voices in the history of music! Rolling Stone named her the World's Greatest Living Entertainer in 2022, and one of the Greatest Vocalists of All Time in 2023! She is the most awarded musician in Grammys history, with 35 wins during her career! All 8 of her solo studio albums debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200 with 9 singles reaching No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 as a Solo artist and 13 as a member of Destiny's child! “Irreplaceable” reigned at #1 on the Hot 100 for 10 weeks while “Crazy in Love” reigned for 8! “Texas Hold ‘Em” scored 2 weeks at #1 on the Hot 100, becoming the first country song by a Black woman to top the chart! Beyoncé has championed Black women’s empowerment in her music, and is the most culturally impactful artist alive, inspiring generations and paving the way for many... The New Yorker called her “the most important and compelling popular musician of the 21st century.” Time included her as one of the 100 women who has so far defined the 21st century!

Beyoncé is the most successful black touring act in history, and the first Black artist and 2nd female artist ever to surpass $2 Billion in lifetime touring revenue! She received the Pollstar Touring Artist of the Decade award in 2021 and continues to set touring records, solidifying her status as one of the most successful live performers overall in history. Her 'Renaissance World Tour' (2023) grossed $579.8 million, the highest grossing tour by a female artist at the time and the highest by a Black artist, while her 'Cowboy Carter Tour' earned $407.6 million, the highest-grossing country tour ever and the shortest tour to clear $400M with 32 shows in history! Beyoncé became the first female and first American artist to have 2 tours gross over $400 million, and also holds the record for the most tours by a female artist grossing over $200 million each, with multiple tours achieving this milestone, including The Mrs. Carter Show World Tour ($229.7 million, 2013-2014), The Formation World Tour ($260 million, 2016), The On the Run II Tour with Jay-Z ($254 million, 2018), The Renaissance World Tour ($579.8 million, 2023), and The Cowboy Carter Tour ($407.6 million, 2025). The Cowboy Carter Tour’s five-night stand at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California (April 28–May 9, 2025), grossed $55.7 million with 217,143 tickets sold, making it the biggest reported single-venue engagement by a female artist in Billboard Boxscore history! 

Beyoncé's 2013 Super Bowl XLVII halftime show, featuring a Destiny’s Child reunion, drew 110.8 million viewers, and was one of the most-watched in history! She also brought the house down, performing the national anthem at Super Bowl XXXVIII (2004) and joined Coldplay, blowing everyone away at Super Bowl 50 (2016). In 2018, Beyoncé became the first Black woman to headline Coachella, delivering a historic performance celebrating HBCU culture. It is still the most-viewed Coachella set in the history of YouTube!

Beyoncé revolutionized music distribution with her self-titled album 'Beyoncé' (2013), a surprise drop on iTunes that sold over 800,000 copies in its first weekend, breaking all records. 'Lemonade' (2016) followed as a visual album on HBO, earning critical acclaim and two Grammys! 

Beyoncé is the most-awarded and nominated female artist of all time with 756 wins out of 1367 nominations! She has won 35 Grammy Awards out of 99 nominations and is the most awarded and nominated Artist in history! She has won 30 MTV Video Music Awards, including the 2014 Michael Jackson Video Vanguard Award, making her the joint-most awarded artist in MTV history! She has won 29 Billboard Music Awards including the inaugural Billboard Millennium Award, 2 Billboard R&B/Hip-Hop Awards, a Billboard Latin Music award, 7 Billboard Mid-Year Music Awards & a Billboard Woman In Music Award and is the 3rd most awarded artist in history! She has also won 39 BET Awards, 32 NAACP Image Awards, the most for any artist and 25 Soul Train Music Awards, more than any other artist in the music industry! She has won 20 Guinness World Records, 13 American Music Awards including the International Artist of Excellence award and 4 World Music Awards including the Legend Award for Outstanding Contribution to the Arts! She has also won 5 BRIT Awards, 4 Pollstar Awards, 4 NRJ Awards including Artist of the Decade in 2010, 3 People's Choice Awards and 3 IHeartRadio Awards including the Innovator Award for being a "global cultural icon" who has taken "creative risks, successfully transformed their music and influenced pop culture". In 2025 Beyoncé won an Emmy Award for 'Beyoncé Bowl'! The Recording Industry Association of America named Beyoncé RIAA's Top Certified Artist of the 2000's Decade and Billboard named her the Top Female Artist and Top Radio Songs Artist of the 2000's Decade! 

Beyoncé is also a hugely successful award-winning actress! Her films have contributed more than $3 billion in worldwide box-office revenue, making her the highest-grossing Black singer at the worldwide movie box-office. She has earned numerous prestigious nominations and awards for her acting. In 2022, she was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Original Song for "Be Alive" (from King Richard), a Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Song and a Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song. She was also nominated for a Golden Globe for 'Dreamgirls' (2006). She has won 2 MTV Movie Awards for Best Female Performance for 'Dreamgirls' in 2007 for her role as Deena Jones and Best Fight for 'Obsessed'  in 2010 for her performance as Sharon Charles and 2 BET Awards for Best Actress in 2007 for 'Dreamgirls' and the YoungStars Award in 2020 for her voice acting as Nala in Disney’s The Lion King (2019). She has also won 2 Black Reel Awards for Outstanding Supporting Actress in 2007 for 'Dreamgirls' and Outstanding Original Song in 2020 for “Spirit” from 'The Lion King'. She also won the NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Actress in a Motion Picture in 2007 for 'Dreamgirls'!

Beyoncé is also a very successful businesswoman and one of the wealthiest musical artists! In December 2025, Forbes estimated her net worth to be 1 BILLION, after naming her the annual highest-earning female musician in 2008, 2010, 2014 and 2017. In 2008 she founded Parkwood Entertainment and launched the fashion line Ivy Park with Adidas in 2016, and received the Fashion Icon Award from the Council of Fashion Designers of America that same year! Her self-funded haircare brand, Cécred, is a massive success and now 100% hers, racking up $200M+ in first-year sales and 2M customers in 6 months! It's the Biggest prestige hair launch in Ulta history! Her SirDavis whiskey is also a big hit! 

Beyoncé is also a philanthropist and in 1999, established the Knowles-Rowland Center for Youth. Following Hurricane Katrina in 2005, Beyoncé co-founded the Survivor Foundation to offer transitional housing for displaced families and support the construction of new homes, extending her aid after Hurricane Ike in 2008, and donating $100,000 to the Gulf Coast Ike Relief Fund. In 2007, she launched the Knowles-Temenos Place Apartments, a housing development that accommodates 43 displaced individuals. Beyoncé donated her entire $4 million salary in 2008 from the film Cadillac Records to Phoenix House, a nonprofit focused on drug and alcohol rehabilitation. In 2016, Beyoncé and Jay-Z donated $1.5 million to civil rights organizations including Black Lives Matter, Hands Up United, and the Trayvon Martin Foundation! In August 2017, during Hurricane Harvey, Beyoncé launched BeyGood Houston to support those affected, donated $75,000 worth of new mattresses to survivors and all proceeds of her remix of J Balvin and Willy William's "Mi Gente" to disaster relief efforts in Puerto Rico, Mexico, the U.S., and the Caribbean in response to Hurricane Harvey, Irma, and Maria, as well as the Chiapas and Puebla earthquakes. In April 2020, Beyoncé donated $6 million to the National Alliance on Mental Illness, UCLA, and local community-based organizations to provide mental health and wellness services for essential workers during the COVID-19 pandemic. Beyoncé also supported the Feminist Coalition in the End SARS movement in Nigeria, paying medical costs for injured protestors & legal fees for arrested protestors. Beyoncé is also a fervent supporter of the Anglophone Crisis in Cameroon, ShutItAllDown in Namibia, Zimbabwean Lives Matter in Zimbabwe, and the Rape National Emergency in Liberia. In December 2020, Beyoncé donated $500,000 towards the housing crisis in the U.S. In 2024, she and BeyGood, introduced an annual grant program supporting cosmetology students and professional hair stylists. In January 2025, Beyoncé donated $2.5M to LA fire relief funds during the wildfires in Southern California which grew to 3 Million! She raised $150,000 for Jamaica hurricane relief.  In August 2026 Beyoncé pledged $1 million for Colombia earthquake aid and $200,000 for Indiana flood relief! She also continued salon/scholarship grants through the Cécred × BeyGOOD fund, gave $100,000 to TSU’s Ocean of Soul band, and with Kelly Rowland put $8.4 million into Knowles-Rowland House, a 31-unit supportive-housing project opening in 2026.

 With 8 straight No. 1 solo albums, a record 35 Grammys, stadium tours that reset the box office, a country experiment that topped the Hot 100 and then paid for itself in the hundreds of millions, and a private foundation that still writes checks when the cameras are off, Beyoncé is not just prolific, her brilliance is the rare ability to reinvent herself at the highest level and still win, sell, and give like no one else in her generation!

text:
How about Watergate? I freaking lived across the street from the "Deep Throat" parking garage where Bob Woodward met his secret informant, FBI Associate Director Mark Felt ("Deep Throat") in 1972 and 1973 to uncover the Nixon administration's scandal.

Money laundering was a core mechanism used to fund the Watergate break-in and the subsequent cover-up. 

Re-election officials set up secret, illegal slush funds using corporate donations that were laundered to hide their origins, and they hired political operatives to run sabotage and espionage campaigns against Democratic candidates. This included wiretapping the DNC headquarters.

Sexual blackmail was actively discussed during the investigations and has persisted as a prominent alternative motive. Books like Secret Agenda and Silent Coup argued the true goal of the break-in was to steal a prostitution ring's client list (a "little black book") to look for sexual dirt on politicians or protect figures within the White House.

WikiLeaks released the DNC documents on July 22, 2016, 9 days before Crossfire Hurricane was opened. Then they started releasing batches of John Podesta's hacked personal emails on October 7, 2016 which led to the pizzagate theories. The October 8, 2015 email from PEW's Tamera Luzzatto caught attention despite having no code mentions of pizza.

The leaks also revealed outside public figures frequently emailed Podesta about UFOs. Notably, they included emails from Tom DeLonge attempting to coordinate a meeting about UFO disclosure. In one Jan 2016 email, DeLonge insists to Podesta that despite Major General William Neil McCasland claiming to be a "skeptic," he was actually working closely with DeLonge behind the scenes.

In April 2016, Maltese academic Joseph Mifsud had told Papadopoulos that the Russians had "thousands of emails." This was used as probable cause to open the investigation on July 31, 2016. By hiding Carter Page's lawful cooperation with the CIA, the FBI made Page's interactions with Russians appear illicit, using them to wiretap Page.

In August 2016, Ukrainian anti-corruption investigators discovered a secret, physical "Black Ledger". The ledger recorded $12.7 million in under-the-table, off-the-books cash payments designated for Manafort between 2007 and 2012.

The financial crimes unit that sought the late-2016 (sometime between Sept-Nov) wiretap built their application on their own pre-existing 2014 file, alongside newly intercepted communications from suspected Russian operatives their own intelligence pipelines had discovered.

Manafort was convicted because he hid the millions he was paid by foreign entities, funneled the money through offshore tax havens, and then lied to the FBI to cover up his ongoing ties to Russian intelligence operatives. He was incarcerated from June 2018 – May 2020.

The physical "black ledger" itself had been recovered earlier by anti-corruption groups when the Party of Regions headquarters in Kyiv was ransacked by protesters during the February 2014 Ukrainian revolution. It sat in the hands of investigators and political figures until it was formally turned over to Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and leaked to the media on August 14, 2016. Under pressure, Manafort officially resigned on August 19th.

Some Mr. Manafort’s compensation has remained a mystery, but a "cache of documents discovered after the fall of Mr. Yanukovych’s government may provide some answers," reported the NYT. The papers, known in Ukraine as the “black ledger,” were a chicken-scratch of Cyrillic covering about 400 pages taken from books once kept in a third-floor room in the former Party of Regions headquarters on Lipskaya Street in Kiev.

The documents revealed that Mr. Manafort and several partners had started a fund in 2007 in which Russian oligarch Oleg Deripaska was a major backer. The "Black Ledger" was also used to investigate a massive web of other crimes, primarily inside Ukraine.

The FBI and international financial investigators used the names of the shell companies discovered in the ledger to track down international money laundering networks that had been quietly moving tens of millions of dollars out of Eastern Europe and into Western banks. I wonder what else they found?

Salesforce first signed a contract with Backpage in late 2013 unti the FBI shut it down in April 2018. Court documents note that the Salesforce infrastructure directly facilitated Backpage's "exponential growth," allowing it to scale its platform efficiently into an international powerhouse. From 2013 to 2015 alone, Backpage’s gross revenue skyrocketed to $346 million, nearly $340 million of which was from adult advertising.

text:
The Manchester Evening News piece, written by Patrick Austen-Hardy, weaves together several threads of the summer window's closing hours into a single narrative that touches on transfer market chain reactions, a career at a significant crossroads, and one of the more painful chapters in the modern history of a Premier League footballer's personal experience at a major club. The Zirkzee-Zaha-Roma connection is, on the surface, a straightforward pivot story — one target unavailable, another identified as an alternative — but the full context of Wilfried Zaha's career arc and his United history gives the piece considerably more texture than a standard transfer update.

曼彻斯特晚报这篇由帕特里克·奥斯汀-哈迪撰写的报道，将夏季窗口尾声的多条线索编织成一条叙事主线，触及了转会市场的连锁反应、一段正处于重大十字路口的职业生涯，以及一位英超球员在顶级俱乐部个人经历中最痛苦的篇章之一。表面上，济尔克泽-扎哈-罗马的连接是一个直截了当的目标替换故事——一个目标无法得手，另一个随即被识别为备选——但扎哈职业生涯轨迹的完整背景及其曼联历史，赋予了这篇报道远超常规转会简讯的深度与质感。

The transfer chain mechanics here are worth unpacking carefully. Roma's pursuit of Zirkzee had been building throughout the summer, with the Dutchman also attracting attention from Juventus and Napoli. The fact that moves to all three Italian clubs collapsed — leaving Zirkzee at Manchester United as the window closed — is itself a revealing commentary on either the player's own situation, United's valuation, or both. For Roma specifically, the failure to land Zirkzee has created a positional gap on the left wing that Gasperini is now attempting to fill, and Zaha's availability as a free agent makes him a low-risk, low-cost solution to a problem that emerged from circumstances outside the club's control. Gazzetta dello Sport's framing of Zaha as fitting Gasperini's requirement for a winger who can cut inside from the left is tactically coherent — that has been the defining characteristic of Zaha's game throughout his Palace years, a movement pattern that produced 68 goals and 30 assists across 291 Premier League appearances for the south London club.

这里的转会连锁机制值得仔细拆解。罗马对济尔克泽的追逐贯穿整个夏天，这位荷兰人同样吸引了尤文图斯和那不勒斯的关注。三家意大利俱乐部的收购全部告吹——济尔克泽在窗口关闭时仍留守曼联——这本身就是对球员处境、曼联估值，或两者兼而有之的一个颇具启示性的注解。就罗马而言，未能签下济尔克泽在左翼制造了一个位置空缺，加斯佩里尼现在试图填补，而扎哈作为自由球员的可签约身份使其成为一个低风险、低成本的解决方案，用以应对一个因俱乐部无法控制的情况而生的问题。《米兰体育报》将扎哈定位为契合加斯佩里尼对左路内切型边锋需求的球员，在战术层面具有充分合理性——这恰恰是扎哈在水晶宫岁月中最具标志性的比赛特征，这一运动模式在他代表南伦敦俱乐部出战的291场英超比赛中创造了68球30助攻。

Roma's familiarity with Zaha is not new intelligence either. The Giallorossi had previously explored signing him in the summer of 2023, before he ultimately moved to Galatasaray. That prior interest means this is not a cold approach built on desperation but a reconnection with a player they have assessed before and evidently maintained positive views on. The fact that the earlier deal did not materialise was a circumstance of timing rather than a negative evaluation, which means Gasperini's staff are not starting their due diligence from scratch.

罗马对扎哈的熟悉程度也并非新情报。黄红军曾在2023年夏天探索过签下他，然而他最终转投加拉塔萨雷。此前的兴趣意味着这并非建立在绝望之上的仓促接触，而是与他们之前已评估过、并显然保持积极看法的球员重续前缘。早期交易未能实现是时机使然，而非负面评估的结果，这意味着加斯佩里尼的团队无需从零开始尽职调查。

Zaha's post-Galatasaray career trajectory is, however, a genuine question mark that hangs over this transfer speculation. His time at the Turkish club was far from settled: one full season in Istanbul, a loan to Lyon in the summer of 2024, a return to Galatasaray in January, another loan — this time to Charlotte FC in MLS — just over a week later, and then an official release this summer. That is a restless and somewhat turbulent sequence for a player of his stature, and the fact that Crystal Palace, his spiritual home as a footballer, chose not to re-sign him despite his training with the club throughout the summer is the most telling signal of all. Palace know Zaha better than any club in world football; if they assessed his current physical condition and decided against bringing him back, that is an evaluation that any prospective employer must weigh carefully.

然而，扎哈离开加拉塔萨雷后的职业生涯轨迹是悬在这场转会猜测之上真实存在的问号。他在土耳其俱乐部的时光远谈不上稳定：伊斯坦布尔一个完整赛季，2024年夏天租借里昂，一月回归加拉塔萨雷，一周多之后再次出发——这次以租借形式加盟美职联球队夏洛特，然后今夏被正式解约。对于一位有着他这般地位的球员而言，这是一段躁动且略显动荡的经历。而最能说明问题的信号，是水晶宫——作为球员意义上他精神家园的球队——在他整个夏天随队训练之后选择不重新签约。世界上没有哪家俱乐部比水晶宫更了解扎哈；如果他们评估了他目前的身体状况后决定不把他带回，这是任何潜在雇主都必须审慎权衡的判断。

The United dimension of this story, however briefly treated in the article, remains the most emotionally resonant part of Zaha's broader narrative. The detail that he only made two Premier League appearances for United, earning 28 minutes of game time under David Moyes before a loan to Cardiff and then a return to Palace under Van Gaal, is well documented. But the 2018 interview quoted in the piece adds dimensions that statistics alone cannot capture. Zaha's account of dealing with malicious rumours at 19, living alone in Manchester without the support structures provided to other players, without a car, cut off from family, and managing the psychological weight of those circumstances by himself, is a deeply human portrait of what the experience of being a young footballer at the wrong club at the wrong time can look like. The specific grievance that nobody at United attempted to clear up the false rumours circulating about him speaks to an institutional failure of pastoral care that goes well beyond footballing matters. That he emerged from that period with the resilience he later demonstrated at Palace is, in retrospect, a remarkable personal achievement.

这篇报道中关于曼联的部分，尽管篇幅简短，仍是扎哈更宏观叙事中情感共鸣最为深沉的部分。他在曼联仅出场两次英超联赛、在大卫·莫耶斯麾下获得28分钟上场时间、随后租借加的夫、又在范加尔执教期间重返水晶宫——这些细节均有案可查。但文章引用的2018年专访为单纯的数据所无法呈现的维度增添了血肉。扎哈讲述自己在19岁时独自在曼彻斯特应对恶意谣言的经历——没有提供给其他球员的支持体系，没有车，与家人天各一方，独自承受那些心理重压——是一幅深刻的人性画像，描绘了一个年轻球员在错误时间置身错误俱乐部是何种面貌。他明确表达的委屈在于，曼联没有任何人试图澄清围绕他流传的不实谣言，这揭示了一种远超足球事务范畴的人文关怀制度性失职。他从那段经历中展现出的韧性，以及此后在水晶宫的表现，回望之下是一项非凡的个人成就。

The free agent status that now defines Zaha's situation is the final chapter of a career that has had more twists than most. At 33, and with his post-Palace trajectory pointing to diminishing returns at the elite level, a move to Roma under a tactically ambitious manager like Gasperini could represent a meaningful final chapter — a coach who can extract specific utility from a winger of his profile and a city whose footballing culture may suit him better than Istanbul or Charlotte did. Whether Gasperini's interest translates into a formal offer, and whether Zaha's current condition meets Roma's requirements, remains to be seen. But the connection, rooted in both tactical logic and a prior relationship between club and player, has a coherence that makes it more than idle speculation.

扎哈目前自由球员的身份，是一段经历了远比大多数球员更多转折的职业生涯最后一章。33岁的他，离开水晶宫后的轨迹指向顶级水平上逐渐递减的回报，而在加斯佩里尼这样一位战术雄心勃勃的主帅麾下加盟罗马，或许代表着一个有意义的收尾篇章——一位能够从他这种类型边锋身上挖掘特定价值的教练，以及一座足球文化或许比伊斯坦布尔或夏洛特更适合他的城市。加斯佩里尼的兴趣能否转化为正式报价，扎哈目前的状态能否达到罗马的要求，尚待观察。但这一连结，植根于战术逻辑与俱乐部和球员之间的前缘，具备的合理性使其远不止于空穴来风的猜测。

The Cinematic Cuck: How George Clooney Became Hollywood's Most Vain and Vacuous Parasite

George Clooney is the perfect specimen of Hollywood's rotting soul, a second-rate actor who has spent three decades playing the role of concerned citizen while embodying everything contemptible about coastal elite arrogance. Look at this creature, this Nespresso salesman in a tuxedo, who has built an entire post-career identity on lecturing working Americans about their carbon footprints while his private jets crisscross the Atlantic like airborne hypocrisies. He admits his climate activism is undercut by his own travel, calls it a "personal weakness," and expects applause for the confession. This is not honesty; this is the calculated humility of a man who knows no consequence will follow. He will keep flying, keep emitting, keep collecting his millions from European luxury brands, and keep telling you to bike to work.

The viciousness beneath the veneer emerged early and never stopped. In 2003, with Charlton Heston dying of Alzheimer's, Clooney joked about the diagnosis at an awards ceremony and when criticized, sneered that Heston "deserves whatever anyone says about him" because he headed the NRA. This is the true face: mocking a conservative icon's terminal illness because he disagreed with his politics. He later claimed it was a joke and offered a private apology, but the mask had slipped. He called George W. Bush "just dim," compared his administration to The Sopranos, and spent the Iraq War era posing as a foreign policy expert while his actual expertise began and ended with reading lines written by others. His 2005 film "Good Night, and Good Luck" was not art; it was a partisan hit job disguised as historical drama, McCarthyism analogized to Bush-era counterterrorism with all the subtlety of a sledgehammer.

His Darfur activism followed the same pattern: simplistic moralizing about complex conflicts, celebrity briefings at the UN that produced nothing but photo opportunities, and the reduction of African civil wars to good-versus-evil narratives that outsiders could solve with enough hashtags and satellite imagery. 

Conservatives initially dismissed it as Bush-bashing; some later praised his persistence, but the fundamental critique remained. Celebrity activism is not policy. It is ego masquerading as expertise, and Clooney has made it his second career.

The financial hypocrisy is breathtaking. He raised fifteen million dollars for Obama in 2012, another fifteen million for Hillary Clinton in 2016, and called the sums "obscene" while pocketing the access and influence. He agreed with Bernie Sanders about money in politics even as he vacuumed it up. This is not principle; this is performance. He plays the conscience-stricken liberal for interviewers and the power-broker for politicians, collecting chits from both sides while delivering nothing to the causes he claims to champion. In June 2024, he co-hosted a fundraiser that raised twenty-eight to thirty million dollars for Joe Biden, then weeks later published a New York Times op-ed declaring that the Biden he saw was "not the same man" and that Democrats could not win with him. Trump called it turning on "Crooked Joe like the rats they both are," and the description fits. 

Clooney took the money, posed for the photos, then knifed the candidate when convenient, later admitting that replacing Biden with Harris was a "mistake" because she had to run against her own record. He engineered a loss and then distanced himself from it, the Hollywood equivalent of taking credit for the greenlight and blaming the director for the bomb.

His Trump obsession has become clinical. He called Trump a "xenophobic fascist" in 2016, predicted Americans would reject him, and has spent every subsequent year proving himself wrong while doubling down. He called Trump a "Hollywood elitist" collecting a SAG pension, a projection so transparent it requires no analysis. In 2026, he called an Iran-related threat a potential war crime, prompting the White House to respond that Clooney commits "war crimes" with his movies. He told ABC and CBS they should have told Trump "go f*** yourself" instead of settling lawsuits, and accused Bari Weiss of dismantling CBS News. This is not political commentary; this is tantrum masquerading as insight, the ravings of a man who cannot accept that his predictions failed and his influence waned.

The French citizenship is the final punchline. After years of criticizing America, after calling Trump a fascist and predicting national decline, Clooney and his family received French citizenship in late 2025, settling into their Provence estate with the ease of people who have never depended on the nations they lecture. Trump posted that it was "good news," calling them "two of the worst political prognosticators of all time," and Clooney responded by agreeing America should be made great again "starting in November." The exchange revealed everything: a wealthy critic of America seeking European refuge, a man who treats citizenship as a lifestyle accessory, a "progressive" who flees to a country with its own immigration and crime problems because the taxes are lower and the wine is better. A French official questioned the "double standard" given Clooney's limited French; the question answers itself.

Clooney is not a civic-minded Democrat from Kentucky. He is a cosmopolitan parasite who treats politics as another Hollywood production, high-minded rhetoric and personal attacks with no accountability when outcomes disappoint. He is the perfect example of what has destroyed the left: unelected power wielded by people who have never built anything, never risked anything, never suffered the consequences of their prescriptions. He is smug, he is vicious, he is hypocritical, and he is ultimately irrelevant, a man whose cultural moment passed while he was still posing for the cameras. His career is a warning: fame is not wisdom, wealth is not virtue, and the most beautiful people can be the most rotten inside.

How Portland Breaks the Doom Loop

Revised September 4, 2026 — second revision, all data points re-verified against primary sources

Bottom line

Portland does not escape by finding enough money to preserve every existing institution. It escapes by becoming visibly competent at the things residents, families, workers, and employers experience every day: public order, schools, housing, permitting, taxes, and basic services.

The central mistake is treating population loss, declining school enrollment, downtown weakness, and budget deficits as separate problems. They reinforce one another:

High costs and weak services reduce confidence → families and employers leave or avoid Portland → enrollment, investment, and the tax base weaken → fixed costs are spread across fewer people → government raises taxes or cuts visible services → confidence falls again.

Each link in that chain has a data point behind it. Housing cost is a documented driver of out-migration from the state and the region—Census migration analysis in March 2026 found Oregon losing residents in their prime earning years, in part because housing is too expensive. Week (Mar 2026) PPS is losing roughly 700–800 students a year as its K-12 base shrinks, which is the tax-base leg of the loop in the most concrete form a city can see. PPS/PSU forecast Office vacancy above 27% keeps the business-license-tax base soft even as the city forecasts a $66.9 million General Fund shortfall. CBRE

Portland must reverse that sequence. It needs a four-year recovery program that protects essential services, cuts institutional overhead, restores consequences for destructive behavior, makes room for families, and measures agencies by outcomes rather than intentions.

The city is damaged, not dead

The decline is real, but it is no longer accurate to describe every indicator as being in uninterrupted free fall.

Multnomah County had an estimated 795,391 residents in 2025—about 2.5% fewer than its 2020 base of 815,400—but gained about 919 residents between July 2024 (794,472) and July 2025. That is stabilization, not recovery: the county lost roughly 20,000 people from 2020 to 2025 and has gained fewer than 1,000 in the most recent year. U.S. Census Bureau
Portland's overall office vacancy rate was 27.0% in the second quarter of 2026, down 20 basis points from the prior quarter, but still above year-ago levels. The Total Downtown submarket was 36.5% vacant. CBRE Q2 2026
The City's December forecast puts the FY 2026–27 General Fund shortfall at $66.9 million: a $50 million one-time gap plus a $16.9 million ongoing gap. The ongoing number is the one that matters structurally; the one-time piece is largely expiring one-time funding. City of Portland
Portland Public Schools anticipates an approximately $50 million structural budget deficit for 2026–27, following an additional $40 million in reductions the previous year. The district frames this as a multi-year problem, not a one-time cut cycle. PPS, PPS budget FAQ
PPS enrollment is projected to fall from 43,375 students in 2024–25 to about 37,181 in 2034–35 under the medium forecast—a decline of roughly 6,200 students, or 14.3%. That is about a fifth of the district gone in a decade. PPS/PSU forecast
Portland's own 2026–30 housing plan reports 10,526 people in Multnomah County's 2025 point-in-time count (night of January 22, 2025)—up 67% from 2023—of whom 2,037 were counted unsheltered on the streets and a further 5,090 were presumed unsheltered from the county's by-name list. A broader April 2025 administrative count recorded 14,864 people, including 6,796 unsheltered. Different definitions explain the different totals; either measure shows a crisis on a scale that affects daily public life. City housing plan, FY 2026–27 action plan

These numbers describe a city with valuable neighborhoods, infrastructure, employers, universities, and cultural assets—but one that has made itself unusually expensive while allowing core public systems to lose credibility.

The school crisis is both demographic and institutional

Fewer births and smaller incoming cohorts are unavoidable facts. Expensive housing and an inventory dominated by small units also make Portland less suitable for families. But PPS is not merely a passive victim of demography. Schools compete with suburbs, private schools, charter schools, homeschooling, and the decision not to live inside the district at all.

That means enrollment is partly a confidence measure.

PPS performs above Oregon's weak statewide averages: the district reports 56.4% reading proficiency against a 43.0% state average, 48.0% math proficiency against 31.2%, and an 82.5% four-year graduation rate (70.3% for the most underserved groups, by its own reporting). Those results disprove the cartoon that nothing works. They do not constitute a compelling value proposition when nearly half of students are not proficient in reading, slightly more than half are not proficient in math, and families face high housing and tax costs to remain in the district. PPS academic dashboard

The trust argument belongs in the analysis, and it should be stated precisely as a trust problem rather than an accusation. Hair color or sexual orientation does not close a school; policy preferences and institutional priorities can. When parents read board agendas, communications, and budget priorities and conclude that ideological program questions get more visible attention than literacy, mathematics, discipline, attendance, and classroom safety, some families vote with their feet. The district's own public materials lean hard on academic recovery and transparency, which is exactly what a system trying to win back families should be doing—but the perception problem is real and it costs enrollment. Whether every individual perception is fair is beside the operational point: a public system that requires voluntary family participation must earn trust, and trust is earned in classrooms first.

The solution is not to ban every discussion somebody dislikes. It is to establish a clear hierarchy: academic mastery, safety, truthfulness, and viewpoint neutrality come first. Social programs survive only if legally required or demonstrably useful to those goals.

The recovery program

1. Restore public order—with shelter, treatment, and consequences

Portland cannot market its way around visible disorder. Parents and employers respond to what they encounter, not citywide averages or explanations.

The city should:

Offer a real shelter or treatment pathway, then consistently enforce prohibitions on camping, open drug use, vandalism, theft, threats, and obstruction of sidewalks.
Concentrate police, behavioral-health clinicians, prosecutors, and sanitation teams on a small number of chronic hot spots and repeat offenders rather than dispersing responsibility.
Create staffed alternative placements for people who cannot safely remain in ordinary shelters because of acute addiction, psychosis, or violent behavior.
Publish one weekly dashboard showing unsheltered homelessness, shelter capacity, placements into treatment or housing, overdose calls, repeat arrests, reported crime, cleanup time, and the number of people returning to the street.
Make city and county leaders jointly accountable. Residents should not have to understand jurisdictional charts to learn why a tent, dealer, or dangerous individual remains outside a school or business.

Compassion without functioning limits abandons both the public and the person deteriorating on the street. Enforcement without sufficient shelter and treatment merely moves the problem. Portland needs both.

2. Make PPS a school system families actively choose

School consolidation is necessary when enrollment falls, but closing buildings is accounting—not reform. PPS itself has acknowledged that operating the same number of buildings with fewer students is a driver of its deficit. The surviving schools must become noticeably better. PPS budget explanation

The district should adopt the following compact:

Protect the classroom first. Ring-fence instructional days, K–3 literacy, mathematics, special education, advanced coursework, career and technical education, and school-level safety staff before protecting central-office initiatives.
Audit the bureaucracy publicly. List every central-office unit, consultant contract, program mandate, and non-school position with its cost, legal basis, and measurable student outcome. Eliminate or consolidate work that cannot show one.
Use objective measures. Keep annual standardized assessments, report proficiency and growth by school, and publish comparable attendance, discipline, graduation, and postsecondary-readiness data. Tests are incomplete measures; removing them does not remove inequality or failure.
Restore classroom order. Establish a districtwide behavior code with predictable consequences. Chronically violent or severely disruptive students need well-staffed alternative settings—not repeated returns to classrooms where everyone else loses instruction.
Give parents meaningful choice. Expand open enrollment, focus-option and magnet programs, charter capacity, and transportation access. Allow successful schools to grow. Require persistently failing schools to adopt a proven turnaround model, change operators, or close.
Make curriculum transparent. Parents should be able to inspect curricula and age-sensitive materials easily. Political and moral questions should be taught accurately and without compelled ideological agreement.
Staff for actual enrollment. Negotiate labor rules that allow staffing and facilities to adjust predictably with student counts while protecting strong teachers rather than preserving every historical position or building.

School closures should follow published criteria: building condition, utilization, academic performance, transportation burden, neighborhood growth potential, program uniqueness, and operating cost. The district should announce the full multi-year map once, provide transition support, and stop reopening the fight annually.

3. Build a city for children, not merely units

Portland has made useful reforms. It permitted more than 1,400 accessory-dwelling and middle-housing units between August 1, 2021 and June 30, 2024 in single-dwelling zones—middle housing is now the most common housing type built there—and in July 2025 the city adopted a temporary SDC exemption for new housing units issued between August 15, 2025 and September 30, 2028, with a target of 5,000 units. City of Portland, SDC exemption

But unit count alone is not a family policy. Portland should:

Preapprove designs for two-, three-, and four-bedroom townhouses, courtyard apartments, duplexes, and small detached homes.
Guarantee a decision deadline for code-compliant housing applications; missing the deadline should trigger automatic escalation and fee refunds.
Extend fee relief only for projects that begin construction on schedule—the SDC exemption's 12-month foundation/inspection requirement is the right pattern; make it universal so exemptions cannot become land speculation.
Permit schools, churches, and nonprofits to build family housing on underused land.
Sell or lease surplus public land and closed-school sites for housing, childcare, or community uses through transparent auctions and performance conditions.
Prioritize safe routes to school, usable parks, libraries, and clean commercial streets in neighborhoods targeted for family housing.

The relevant metric is not merely units permitted. It is the number of households with children that can and do remain in Portland.

4. Stop increasing the price of staying

Portland-area taxpayers face overlapping governments and taxes. Businesses operating in Portland can encounter a 2.6% city business license tax, a 2% Multnomah County business income tax, and a 1% Metro supportive-housing business income tax (applies to businesses with gross receipts above $5 million), each with different bases and thresholds. High-income residents also face Metro's 1% supportive-housing personal income tax and Multnomah County's Preschool for All tax of 1.5% above $125,000 (single) / $200,000 (joint), rising to 3% above $250,000 / $400,000—and the county has already scheduled a further increase to as much as 3.8% beginning January 2027. All of this sits on top of Oregon income tax. City revenue rates, Metro tax, Preschool for All

Two honesty points belong in any tax discussion. First, the individual rates are not the highest in the country—some peer cities layer more on businesses—but Oregon taxpayers stack these on top of a state income tax with no state or local sales tax, so the effective cumulative burden on wage income is what drives decisions, and the administrative complexity (three revenue authorities, different bases, different thresholds) is a real friction cost in itself. Second, the Preschool for All scheduled increase in 2027 is a live example of exactly the pattern this section targets: a new rate increase that the marginal household feels before the program's value is felt.

For four years, Portland, Multnomah County, and Metro should agree to:

No new broad-based taxes, rate increases, or major fees without an offset elsewhere.
One filing portal, harmonized definitions, and one audit for local business and personal income taxes.
Independent performance audits of homelessness, preschool, clean-energy, and economic-development spending.
Automatic sunset reviews for new programs and contracts.
A requirement that structural deficits be addressed with recurring savings—not temporary money or optimistic forecasts.

The City should use zero-based review on administrative and discretionary spending while protecting police response, fire, streets, parks, permitting, and sanitation. Do not solve a shrinking tax base by making the remaining base easier to leave.

5. Rebuild downtown as a place to conduct business

Remote work caused much of the initial office shock, but policy determines whether downtown captures the recovery. Q2 2026 showed modest real signs—114,831 square feet of positive net absorption in the quarter itself (though year-to-date net absorption was still negative at −201,564 sq ft, a 392,000-sq-ft improvement over the same period last year), overall vacancy down 20 basis points to 27.0%, and zero square feet of office under construction—which is exactly the kind of trend that is worth protecting, not something to ignore in a panic. CBRE Q2 2026

Portland should:

Create clean-and-safe zones with explicit response-time standards for trash, graffiti, camping, public drug use, and threatening behavior.
Offer temporary, performance-based tax abatements for net new downtown employment and ground-floor occupancy—not subsidies for merely moving jobs from another Portland neighborhood.
Simplify change-of-use rules for older office buildings. Residential conversion will work for only a subset, but government should not make feasible projects impossible.
Allow inexpensive temporary uses—education, studios, light production, entertainment, childcare, and pop-up retail—in distressed buildings.
Accelerate foreclosure, receivership, or sale when absentee owners leave dangerous buildings vacant.
Recruit many midsize employers instead of waiting for one trophy headquarters.

Downtown does not need to become what it was in 2019. It does need enough residents, students, workers, customers, and enforcement to sustain ordinary street life.

Governance: one scorecard, named owners, automatic consequences

Portland's fragmented government makes failure easy to explain and difficult to own. The mayor, council, county chair, Metro president, and PPS superintendent should sign a public recovery compact with quarterly reporting.

A word about feasibility: Oregon's intergovernmental structure means a voluntary compact across city, county, Metro, and the school district has no enforcement mechanism of its own. It is an accountability device, not a contract—its power comes from the quarterly public scorecard making every named owner's performance legible to voters, not from any legal compulsion. That's why the scorecard and the public reporting are the actual mechanism; the signature is the commitment. If the compact fails to produce quarterly reports for two consecutive quarters, that should be treated as the program's first measurable failure.

The scorecard should contain no more than 15 measures:

Net domestic migration and households with children
PPS kindergarten capture and total enrollment
Reading and mathematics proficiency and growth
Chronic absenteeism and serious classroom incidents
Central-office cost per student
Unsheltered homelessness and repeat homelessness
Shelter utilization and exits to stable housing or treatment
Overdose deaths and calls
Reported violent and property crime, plus response times
Housing permits, completions, and median approval time
Downtown foot traffic, ground-floor vacancy, and office vacancy
Net business formation and downtown employment
Recurring budget gap and reserves

Every program should have an owner, target, deadline, and predetermined response to failure. If a contractor misses outcome targets, rebid the work. If a bureau misses permit deadlines, refund fees and change management. If a school remains unsafe or academically stagnant, intervene rather than rename the initiative.

Sequence

First 100 days

Freeze new taxes and discretionary programs.
Publish the consolidated recovery scorecard and complete spending inventories.
Establish hot-spot public-order teams and shelter availability reporting.
Publish PPS's complete school-consolidation criteria and central-office audit.
Adopt guaranteed permit timelines and preapproved family-housing designs.

First year

Consolidate schools and sell or repurpose unused property.
Move money from administration into literacy, math, special education, school safety, and alternative placements.
Harmonize local tax administration.
Enforce public-space rules consistently after shelter offers.
Launch downtown occupancy and employment incentives tied to verified net growth.

Years two through four

Expand family-sized housing and successful public-school options.
Reduce recurring deficits without across-the-board service degradation.
Drive unsheltered homelessness and chronic hot spots materially downward.
Restore positive domestic migration, PPS kindergarten capture, and private investment.

What will not work

Another tax increase without institutional reform. It temporarily fills a hole while worsening the incentive to leave. The Preschool for All's scheduled 2027 rate increase is the live version of this error.
Across-the-board cuts. They protect failed priorities and weaken competent services equally.
Closing schools without improving the survivors. Families do not return because the district operates fewer buildings.
Housing-only or enforcement-only homelessness policy. Portland needs shelter, treatment, housing, and consequences working together.
Treating parental distrust as misinformation. Publish the curriculum, finances, discipline data, and outcomes; then earn trust.
Waiting for births or office work to rebound. Portland must compete for the families, employers, and workers that still have choices.
Replacing delivery with moral branding. Equity, compassion, sustainability, and inclusion are not measurable results. Safe streets, literate students, completed housing, stable placements, and functioning budgets are.

Verdict

The provocative critique is substantially closer to the truth than a purely demographic explanation: Portland's culture of governance helped produce the policies, costs, disorder, and institutional priorities that accelerated family and business flight. The crude identity shorthand is not the causal variable; the governing choices associated with that political culture are.

The evidence now supports the "damaged, not dead" framing more comfortably than it did a year ago: county population has turned marginally positive, office vacancy is improving off the bottom, and middle-housing production is real. But stabilization is not recovery. Every counter-trend is small against the structural base—enrollment still falling at roughly 700 students a year, a $16.9 million ongoing city gap, a ~14% decade-long district enrollment cliff, and a homeless count up two-thirds in two years. The margin for error is thin.

Portland still has enough wealth, talent, neighborhoods, infrastructure, and civic attachment to recover. But recovery requires a visible change in hierarchy:

Results before process. Classrooms before administration. Shelter and treatment before tolerated disorder. Families and employers before institutional self-preservation.

If Portland demonstrates that hierarchy consistently for several years, the loop reverses: confidence produces investment, families and students stabilize the tax base, fixed costs become manageable, and improving services attract more confidence. There is no single silver bullet—but there is a clear order of operations.
